headline: Deep models predict regulatory, mutational, and drug-response outcomes from omics data
label: Deep Learning Biological Prediction
summary: Transformer and CNN architectures now predict regulatory, mutational, and drug-response endpoints from sequence and multi-omics inputs in recent preprints and…
synthesis: The common thread is deep networks trained to predict hard-to-measure biological outcomes directly from sequence or multi-omics inputs. Examples span transcription factor binding (EpiBinder), base-pair mutation risk and non-coding driver flagging (MutFormer), chromatin accessibility and histone marks from sequence plus trans-regulator expression (Corgi), and cancer drug response from multi-omics with cross-attention (ProphDR, DL4DR). Cell-free DNA appears in UNITE, which compares XGBoost and CNN models on 0.1x shallow whole-genome sequencing, and in GeneLLM, which models plasma cfRNA nucleotide reads without gene quantification. What is new is breadth of input representation: LEAF-1 pre-trains a fragment-level foundation model on roughly 58 billion DNA fragments, while DeepDETAILS deconvolves bulk profiles into cell-type-specific nascent transcription. Comparative benchmarking is also present, with linear and nonlinear models predicting expression from epigenomes across over 28,000 human genes.
